followup_explanation:
This is a straightforward expository writing task — explaining how ML algorithms improve decision-making, with a request for concise, coherent output. That maps to general knowledge synthesis and instruction-following (note the explicit constraint to be brief and non-rambly).

Dunlin-235B has materially higher scores across the relevant dimensions: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), and Summarization/Creative Generation on the internal evals — all of which bear on producing accurate, well-organized, instruction-compliant prose. These gaps are well outside the noted run-to-run variance.

The query contains nothing harm-adjacent or distasteful, so the only differentiating task-preference dimension between the two models (aversion to graphic/hostile content) doesn't apply here. With that factor neutral, the decision reduces to raw capability, and Dunlin is the stronger model on every relevant benchmark.
